name: list_workspaces
description: List the workspaces you can reach (id, name, deviceId, deviceLabel, accessRole). A workspace with "unavailable" set is one its device no longer serves: sessions cannot start there until the person adds the folder again. A session token reaches every workspace of the person who started it, as at most Member (a session working in an Issue: only the Issue's workspace); start work in another one only when the person asks for it there or the task needs what only that workspace's device has (list_resources).

name: list_resources
description: List what each device you can reach offers sessions (installed browsers, macOS screen control), whether it is online, and the workspaces on it where you may start a session. To use a resource on another device, start a session in one of that device's workspaces (create_session with workspaceId). Resources are the device's own software; nothing is installed for you.

name: list_profiles
description: List the agent profiles you can dispatch to (id, runtime, model, status) on one device: the calling session's device by default, or another device hosting a workspace you reach (see list_workspaces). A profile belongs to its device.

deviceId.description: Device that owns the profiles; defaults to the calling device.

name: list_models
description: List the models a profile can run (its endpoint's catalog), on your device by default or another device hosting a workspace you reach.

deviceId.description: Device that owns the profiles; defaults to the calling device.

name: create_session
description: Create a new Foundry session and deliver it a task. With a session token the new session records you as its parent; in your own workspace (the default) it runs on your device, joins your orchestration group and, without profileId and provider, runs like you. Name workspaceId to start it in another workspace you reach as Member (list_workspaces), on that workspace's device, with your runtime unless you choose a profile there; do that only when the person asked for work there or the task needs a resource only that device has (list_resources). Returns the queued session unless wait=true, which blocks until it settles and returns its response. Parallel sessions writing the same repository race: split independent work and keep one writer per target. To continue an existing session use send_message instead of creating a new one.

prompt.description: The task brief for the new session.

importedContext.description: Background the new session should know before the prompt.

attachments.description: Files to hand over, as a person's attachments arrive: paths of files in your own workspace folder (absolute, or relative to it), or ids (att_…) of attachments your session was given. Foundry copies each, at most 10 files of up to 25 MB each, into the .foundry/attachments folder of the workspace the session runs in, on its device, and lists their paths at the top of the message.

verification.description: Start an independent verifier, to check another session's work. It reads the workspace and runs commands that only read (tests, linters, type checks, git status and diff); the device's sandbox keeps the workspace read-only, so anything that would change it fails, and its commands write only to its own temporary directory outside the workspace. It has no file editing tools and, of the Foundry tools, only those that read; Claude stops after 20 turns per message. A verifier on a device whose worker is older is refused: that device needs a worker update.

forkSessionId.description: Fork: a new session that starts from a copy of this session's native transcript, leaving the source untouched. It runs in the source's workspace, on its device, so you need Member there.

issueId.description: Run inside that Issue's candidate worktree and sandbox; the Issue must be in this workspace and in progress, blocked or verifying. A session working in an Issue starts its sessions there without it.

wait.description: Block until the session settles and return its response.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait, at most 600000 (10 minutes, the default). If the session is still running when it elapses, call wait_session again.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to start the session in, one you reach as Member; defaults to yours with a session token, required without one.

name: handoff_session
description: Start a fresh session that continues another one from facts only: its original goal, last recorded result and status, plus your prompt; never its transcript. Use it instead of forkSessionId when the old transcript is misleading or too long. The source is any session you can read. The new session starts in workspaceId if given (one you reach as Member), else in the source's workspace; without profileId it runs like the source (its profile on the same device, else its runtime). With a session token it records you as its parent.

sessionId.description: The session to continue: an id (sess_…) or a Foundry chat link.

prompt.description: What the new session should do next.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to start the new session in; defaults to the source's.

name: list_sessions
description: List the sessions of one workspace, newest activity first, one line each: id, title, status, runtime, profile, device, workspaceId, parentSessionId, activityAt (and issueId, role, source when set). Yours by default; any workspace you reach with workspaceId. parentSessionId lists the sessions one session started (in that session's workspace unless you name another). Pages of limit sessions; pass the nextCursor a page returns as cursor for the next. Read one session's details with read_context.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to list; defaults to yours with a session token.

parentOnly.description: Only the sessions your session created (needs a session token).

parentSessionId.description: Only the sessions this session (an id or a Foundry chat link) started.

limit.description: Sessions per page; default 30, at most 100.

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page.

name: list_group_sessions
description: List the sessions of one orchestration group in list order, in the same one-line form as list_sessions (a device's native chat in the group has kind native_chat). read_context's summary names a session's group. A replacement orchestrator uses this to take over a group: control does not depend on who started a session.

workspaceId.description: The group's workspace; defaults to yours with a session token.

name: get_session
description: The same compact summary as read_context with scope=summary, of any session or synced native chat you can read in any workspace you reach: title, status and error, runtime/profile/model, device (and whether it is online), workspace, group, times, lineage, event counts, the last input (first 300 characters) and answer (first 1000), the last error event with the events just before it, and background tasks still open in its latest turn. Read events with read_context scope=events.

sessionId.description: A session id (sess_…), a native chat id (native_claude_…, native_codex_…) or a Foundry chat link (https://<host>/chats/<id>?workspace=…).

name: read_context
description: Read a session or native chat you can read, in any workspace you reach, by id or Foundry link. scope=summary (default) is get_session's summary; events lists its events one line each (time | level | label | detail), filtered by levels, labels and query, newest with tail or paged with after/before cursors, within maxBytes; thread (the session's full transcript), transcript (raw native chat) and subagents (the session's native subagents; with taskId, one subagent's transcript) return JSON cut at maxBytes. What a session produced: changes lists the files its own tools wrote and its answers named, one line each with the lines added and removed (with path: that file's diff, the whole session's or one turn's with inputId); file with path reads one of those files as it is now on the session's device; background lists the commands it left running in the background (with taskId: the end of one's output, which needs Member in the session's workspace). Start with summary and events; read thread or transcript only when you need the whole conversation.

sessionId.description: A session id (sess_…), a native chat id (native_claude_…, native_codex_…) or a Foundry chat link (https://<host>/chats/<id>?workspace=…).

levels.description: scope=events: only events of these levels, e.g. ["error","warning"].

labels.description: scope=events: only events with these labels (exact, case-insensitive), e.g. ["Session failed"].

query.description: scope=events: only events whose label, detail or message contains this text (case-insensitive).

tail.description: scope=events: the last N matching events (at most 500). Without it, the first `limit` matches.

limit.description: scope=events: page size without tail; default 50, at most 500.

after.description: scope=events: only events after this cursor, an event id this tool printed or a time (2026-10-09T20:40:00Z).

before.description: scope=events: only events before this cursor, an event id or a time.

context.description: scope=events: also show up to N events (at most 5) just before each match, to see what led to it.

taskId.description: With scope=subagents: the subagent to read. With scope=background: the task whose output to read.

path.description: With scope=changes: the file whose diff to read; with scope=file: the file to read. A path changes lists.

inputId.description: With scope=changes and path: only what that turn (an input id changes lists) changed.

maxBytes.description: Default 12000. events keeps whole lines within it and prints the cursor that continues; background output keeps its end.

name: list_issues
description: List the Issues of one workspace, most recently updated first, one line each: id, shortId, title, status, contract (its state and confirmed revision), run (the status of its latest execution), question (the kind of question waiting for the person, if any) and verified (required criteria passed of total). Yours by default; any workspace you reach with workspaceId. A session working in an Issue sees only that Issue. Read one with get_issue. Issues are read-only here: the person drives them in Foundry.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to list; defaults to yours with a session token.

name: get_issue
description: Read one Issue you can reach: status (and why it is blocked), the person's request, the confirmed contract (revision, goal, scope, constraints and each criterion with its latest verification verdict) and whether a newer draft waits for confirmation, the question waiting for the person, the verification summary and whether the latest review allows acceptance, and its latest execution run (its session id, which read_context reads, status and error).

issueId.description: The Issue's id (iss_…) or short id.

name: send_message
description: Send a message to a session you control: any session in a workspace you reach as Member (a session working in an Issue: only that Issue's sessions), except an Issue's own execution or clarification, which their Issue drives. A running session is steered (Claude adjusts its active turn; Codex queues it for the next one). An idle session takes it as its next input and continues the same native session; profileId/provider/model switch its runtime first (only while it is idle). wait=true blocks until it settles and returns its response.

sessionId.description: An id (sess_…) or a Foundry chat link.

attachments.description: Files to hand over, as a person's attachments arrive: paths of files in your own workspace folder (absolute, or relative to it), or ids (att_…) of attachments your session was given. Foundry copies each, at most 10 files of up to 25 MB each, into the .foundry/attachments folder of the workspace the session runs in, on its device, and lists their paths at the top of the message.

wait.description: Block until the session settles and return its response.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait, at most 600000 (10 minutes, the default). If the session is still running when it elapses, call wait_session again.

name: cancel_session
description: Stop the work a session you control is doing (any session in a workspace you reach as Member; a session working in an Issue: only that Issue's sessions). Cancelling never cascades: sessions it created keep running. The session stays usable: send_message continues it.

sessionId.description: An id (sess_…) or a Foundry chat link.

name: wait_session
description: Block until a session you can read reaches one of the requested statuses (default: completed/failed/canceled) or the timeout elapses, and return it with its response once settled. Prefer this over polling loops.

sessionId.description: An id (sess_…) or a Foundry chat link.

until.description: Statuses to wait for, e.g. ["running"]; default completed, failed and canceled.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait, at most 600000 (10 minutes, the default). If the session is still running when it elapses, call wait_session again.

name: rename_session
description: Rename a session you control (1-120 characters): any session in a workspace you reach as Member (a session working in an Issue: only that Issue's sessions).

sessionId.description: An id (sess_…) or a Foundry chat link.

name: ask_person
description: Ask the person something only they can decide (a choice the confirmed contract leaves open) or allow (a side effect outside the candidate, such as deploying or sending a message). Only an Issue's execution has this tool. After calling it, end your turn with a short summary of where you are; the Issue waits for the person and Foundry resumes you in the same candidate with their answer. Ask one question at a time and never about anything you can decide yourself.

question.description: What you need, in the person's language, with the context they need to answer.

kind.description: input: a decision or information; permission: approval for a specific action. Defaults to input.

options.description: Up to 6 suggested answers; the person may answer otherwise.
